items.definition:
To align or position oneself.
It took him a while to orientate himself in the new city.

To run faster than.
The gazelle managed to outrun the cheetah.

To treat with excessive care and attention.
She loves to pamper herself with a long bath and a good book.

To continue in a course of action despite difficulty.
Despite the setbacks, she continued to persevere with her studies.

to tie (an animal) with a rope or chain so as to restrict its movement
He tethered his horse to a post outside the saloon.

to identify and fix problems
The IT department is trying to troubleshoot the network issue.

to move or cause to move rapidly around and around
The leaves began to whirl in the strong wind.

to destroy, kill, or hit with a sudden burst of energy or force
He used the remote to zap through the channels.

to make friends with someone
She tried to befriend the new student in class.

to make or cause to make a loud, harsh sound
The car horn began to blare loudly.

expose the falseness or hollowness of (a myth, idea, or belief)
The scientist tried to debunk the popular myth.

(of time) pass or go by
Many years will elapse before we meet again.

divide into two parts of equal or nearly equal size
The company decided to halve its production costs.

to speak in a low, unclear voice
He began to mutter to himself as he walked away.

to grant citizenship to; to adapt to a new environment
After living in the country for many years, she decided to naturalize.

to trick someone into giving away personal information online
Scammers may phish for your passwords through fake links.

to elect again
The mayor hopes to be reelected for another term.

to burn or scorch the surface of something with sudden, intense heat
Sear the steak on high heat to lock in the juices.

to change direction suddenly, especially to avoid hitting something
The car swerved to avoid the deer.

to lose or cause to lose luster, especially as a result of exposure to air or moisture
The silver began to tarnish after a few months.

to overbalance or cause to overbalance and fall
The strong winds threatened to topple the old tree.

To remove a program or software from a computer.
I need to uninstall this old software to free up space.

To attach or stick something to something else.
Please affix a stamp to the envelope.

to touch or stroke gently or lovingly
He gently caressed her cheek.

to irritate intensely; to infuriate
His constant complaining began to exasperate me.

to focus intently or obsessively
He tends to fixate on small details.

to regard or represent as perfect or better than in reality
She tended to idealize her childhood.

To severely damage by tearing or crushing.
The machine mangled the fabric beyond repair.

To think about (a fact, proposal, or request) deeply and at length.
She needed time to mull over the job offer.

to set or adjust in advance
Make sure to preset the alarm for 6 AM.

to assign again or to a different person or task
They decided to reassign the project to a new team.

to buy something back
The company decided to repurchase its own shares.

to repost or forward a message on Twitter
She asked her followers to retweet her announcement.

examine closely
The police will scrutinize the evidence carefully.

sing or play music for someone
He decided to serenade her under her window.

spend a lot of money
I decided to splurge on a new pair of shoes.

be full of things; swarm
The pond was teeming with fish.

to bark with a high-pitched sound
The small dog would yap excitedly whenever someone came to the door.

to cut off (a limb or other appendage of the body)
The doctors had to amputate his leg after the accident.

to verify the identity or genuineness of
You need to authenticate your account before proceeding.

to lie exposed to warmth or light, typically from the sun, for relaxation and pleasure
The cat loved to bask in the sun on the windowsill.

to concentrate (control or power) in a central organization
The company decided to centralise all its operations in one office.

to crush (something, typically paper or cloth) so that it becomes creased and wrinkled
He watched the paper crumple in his hand.

to spoil the appearance of
The accident left him with a scar that would disfigure his face.

to prove to be false
Scientists are trying to disprove the theory with new evidence.

to surround
The city walls used to encircle the entire town.

to make someone nervous or confused
Don't fluster him with too many questions.

to move or act quickly
They hastened to finish the work before dark.

to treat with medicine
The doctor decided to medicate the patient for pain.

to state something too strongly; exaggerate
He tends to overstate the difficulties.

to change the corporate image or identity of a company or product
The company decided to rebrand its entire product line.

to rebuke someone, especially officially
The teacher had to reprimand the student for misbehaving in class.

To give a name to (a baby) at baptism as a sign of admission to a Christian Church; to use for the first time.
They decided to christen their new boat "The Wanderer".

To gather into a crowd or mass.
The students began to congregate in the main hall before the assembly.

to surround
Fog began to envelop the city.

to make false
He tried to falsify the financial records.

to make fertile
Farmers fertilize the soil to improve crop yield.

to exchange gunfire
The soldiers had to firefight their way out of the ambush.

to show off
She liked to flaunt her expensive new car.

to wince
He didn't flinch when the loud noise occurred.

to search someone for hidden items
The police officer had to frisk the suspect.

make or become liquid
The intense heat caused the ice to liquefy rapidly.

introduce machines or automatic devices into (a process or place)
The factory decided to mechanize its production line to increase efficiency.

to finance something again, typically with a new loan at a lower rate of interest
They decided to refinance their mortgage to get a better interest rate.
